directive:

A. AUTO ROUTING OFF -> MANUAL. Find the setting that makes ZCode choose the model automatically per thread (the thing that produced 'Model switched Codex (OAuth)/gpt-6.1-sol -> Claude Code (OAuth)/claude-opus-5-5'). Report its exact name, location and current value; if disabling it means editing a config or key under ~/.zcode/**, do NOT edit it - report the exact path, key and proposed value and mark it OWNER-RESERVED, because auth/provider config is owner-only. If it turns out to be a UI toggle with no file, state that plainly. Do not guess; do not change provider/model config.

B. LANE ALLOCATION (your call, within the owner's constraint 'each team a different opencode account, all on space-bunny-free'). Baseline I already sent in D-20261009-023 (DEV acct2, DEVops acct3, PM acct4, COUNCIL chair acct5, COUNCIL second voice new-provider/owen). Now make the ROUTER agree with that allocation: edit .zcode/cliproxy-router.json so each profile prefers the lane alias for its own account (build->opencode-2/, fast->opencode-3/, long-context->opencode-4/, reason->opencode-5/, review->owen/ and keep opencode- out of review), restating the hard drops. For context on why the scoring works: a prefer match is +10 per pattern, so two patterns both matching a lane alias (e.g. 'space-bunny' and 'space-bunny-free') beat a single 'gpt-' match. Verified working output before this revert: build->opencode-2/space-bunny-free, fast->opencode-3, long-context->opencode-4, reason->opencode-5, review->owen, all policy=project. Recreate exactly that, verify all five with the live command, and commit. This is YOUR file to change, not CoS's.

C. STUCK DETECTION - every team must always know when it is stuck. Three signals, one owner (you): (1) MODEL STUCK: a turn that starts and never lands (no reply line and no board final within 20 min of its board start) - record lane id and last error text. (2) PROVIDER STUCK: a 401/403/404/429/timeout on any lane - record which account, which error, whether cooled and for how long; never print a key, only the account label and status. (3) DISCONNECT: a thread whose watcher died (automation fired but no new reply for 2 intervals) or whose session model changed without a directive - record old model, new model, ts. Publish these to .project/dev-loop/PROVIDER-AVAILABILITY.md as a 'Stuck signals' section with a running table, and append one line to .local/staff/desk-stuck.jsonl each time you observe one. Your automation already health-checks the router entrypoint each sweep; make that the trigger that catches a broken lane before a team hits it. A stuck signal must reach Owen through the desk: when you detect one, append a directive to my inbox (coS) stating team, cause, lane, and the one action needed - I relay it, I do not repair auth.

D. Report per item with evidence. Do not push; reply DONE or BLOCKED with the commit, the five verified route outputs, the exact auto-routing setting path/value, and the stuck-signal table seeded with today's real incidents: router entrypoint dead 2026-10-08 01:00 -> 2026-10-09 07:22 (missing module, every command failed), uncommanded model switch 2026-10-07 and again 2026-10-08, and three team stalls where a dead watcher left directives unread for up to 5h.
